meta.about: Krishna Medical Institution Ltd (KIMS) was Incorporated in the year 1973 and is one of the largest corporate healthcare groups in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in terms of patients treated and treatments offered. The company offers multidisciplinary healthcare services with primary, secondary, and tertiary care across 2-3 tier cities and an additional quaternary healthcare facility in tier-1 cities.
meta.keyPoints: Regional Leadership:[1][2] KIMS Hospitals is one of the largest corporate healthcare groups in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, offering multi-disciplinary integrated healthcare with a focus on tertiary and quaternary care at affordable cost. The group today currently runs 26 hospitals across 5 states - Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Kerala (with a 6th state, Tamil Nadu, on the drawing board for Chennai)- and offers 40+ specialty services, including Cardiac Sciences, Oncology, Neuro sciences, Organ Transplantation, and Maternal & Child Health.

accounting.basis: Ind AS, consolidated, one segment. The company's 'EBITDA' includes other income (FY26 ₹828 cr, 21.1% of total income); Screener's operating profit excludes it (₹815 cr, 20.9%). Both are post-Ind AS 116: rent is not deducted (pre-Ind AS EBITDA FY26 ₹785 cr). We use Screener's basis with lease liabilities in net debt.
accounting.doctorFees: Doctors are paid largely as 'consultancy charges' (₹1,007 cr, 25.8% of FY26 revenue, inside other expenses), on top of employee cost (₹682 cr, 17.5%).
accounting.omAccounting: Two kinds of O&M: Kerala's Kannur and Kollam are consolidated as business combinations (KIMS controls them; right-of-use assets ₹186 cr, O&M rights ₹13 cr, contingent consideration ₹56 cr); Sangli, Guntur and Kompally earn a fee ('medical service fees' ₹16.7 cr in FY26) and are outside the bed KPIs. Call options to buy the O&M hospital companies are fair-valued through P&L (−₹3.8 cr FY26, +₹10.8 cr FY25), exercisable from Jan-2027.
accounting.capitalisation: FY26: ₹34 cr of lease interest and ₹21.5 cr of right-of-use depreciation were capitalised into work in progress; this stops as projects open, which is part of why Q1FY27 interest (₹83 cr) and depreciation (₹101 cr) jumped.

accounting.receivables: Receivable days 52 (FY26) vs 28 (FY22); government-scheme receivables were 'a challenge' (CFO, Aug-2026); expected credit loss ₹9.7 cr in FY26.
accounting.minorities: Profit attributable to owners ₹241 cr vs ₹242 cr total in FY26 (minorities' share of profits in Sunshine, Kondapur and Vizag offset by their share of Bengaluru and Nashik losses); ₹30 cr in FY25. Book value of minority interests ₹311 cr (Mar-26).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for KIMS (consolidated, ₹ crore). One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and a post-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin excluding other income (Screener basis: rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest sits in interest and right-of-use depreciation in depreciation; lease liabilities sit in borrowings). The cluster build (five states: beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB, plus O&M fees less eliminations) sits in `businessLines`; the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue and that cluster EBITDA reconciles to model EBITDA. Profit is attributable to owners and the share count is pro forma for the Jun-2026 QIP and the Aug-2026 promoter warrants (fully diluted 42.77 cr; KIMS.patch.js); minority interests (book) sit in net debt and their share of profit in the tax line. Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the cluster build below. FY27 +32%: Q1 +35% (new Kondapur open only 10 days; Palakkad from April), the new Kondapur hospital running ~₹12 cr a month above the old one from July, Bengaluru, Thane and Kerala ramping, and the FY26 base still missing a full year of Mahadevapura and Electronic City. FY28 +20%: occupancy gains at Kondapur, Bengaluru and Kerala (Thrissur O&M from late FY27), ARPOB +4-5% (management guide). FY29 +18%: the Secunderabad replacement block (end-CY27) and Rajahmundry II start. No unannounced acquisitions or greenfields are included. Street: PL ₹5,111 / 6,152 cr, Axis ₹5,264 / 6,222 cr for FY27-28E.

businessLines._why: Revenue by state cluster = average operational beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB (company definitions; the identity reproduces Q1FY27 cluster revenue within ~1%). Telangana: 2,144 operational beds at Jun-26 including ~450 new Kondapur beds (open 10 days) and excluding ~200 Secunderabad beds under rebuild; occupancy dips to 45% in FY27 (Q1 41.1% on the enlarged base; 61-65% on the old base) and recovers as Kondapur fills (management: ~70% in 3-4 years); ARPOB +8% in FY27 (oncology and transplants at Kondapur; Q1 ₹77,009, +10%), then +4-5%. AP: Rajahmundry II adds beds in FY29; ARPOB base ₹26,000-27,000 (management). Maharashtra: Thane and Nashik ramp (Q1 occupancy 58.6%, July Thane revenue ₹21 cr a month). Kerala: Palakkad full year, Thrissur (O&M, 351 beds) from late FY27. Karnataka: ARPOB normalises to ₹80,000-85,000 (management) as empanelments widen; occupancy 33% → 48%. Other = O&M fees (9% of revenue at Sangli, Guntur, Kompally, Arete and Kakinada) less intercompany eliminations (~1% of cluster revenue). Cluster EBITDA margins are on the company basis (including other income); the reconciling line to model EBITDA (other income in cluster figures, O&M fees, classification) runs at −₹33 to −43 cr a year.
businessLines._startupWhy: EBITDA losses of units in their first year or two, already inside the cluster margins (used only for the start-up-adjusted multiple): FY27 Electronic City, Thane (H1), Kondapur transition (old-hospital rent and pre-operative costs), Palakkad and Thrissur start-up ~₹60 cr (management: 'less than half' of FY26's ₹128 cr); FY28 Thrissur and the extra Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ~₹25 cr; FY29 Rajahmundry II and Secunderabad ~₹30 cr.

assumptions._marginWhy: Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin excluding other income (Screener basis): 26% in FY24-25, 20.9% in FY26 (new-unit losses ₹128 cr), 18.9% in Q1FY27 (Q4FY26 19.2%). FY27 20.5%: Bengaluru losses shrink (Q1 −₹19 cr vs Q4FY26 −₹40 cr; cluster guided EBITDA-neutral for the year), Thane breaks even, Nashik positive, offset by the Kondapur transition and Kerala's single-digit margins. FY28 22.0% and FY29 23.5%: new clusters move to mid-teens (Kerala guided mid-teens FY28; Maharashtra 12-15%), Telangana back to ~30%, but new beds at Kondapur, Secunderabad and Rajahmundry keep dragging. Below PL (20.8% / 22.7%) and Axis (22.6% / 23.4%). Rent (Ind AS 116 impact ₹44 cr in FY26, ₹18 cr in Q1FY27) is ~1.5pp of revenue: pre-Ind AS ≈ 19.0% / 20.6% / 22.2%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex plus new leases (right-of-use additions, because lease liabilities are in net debt). FY27 ₹460 cr: Q1 ₹60-75 cr, ₹100-125 cr guided for the next nine months (Secunderabad, Rajahmundry II ₹60-75 cr, residual Kondapur), maintenance ~₹100 cr a year, Thrissur/Palakkad fit-outs and equipment, ~₹60 cr of new leases. FY28 ₹600 cr and FY29 ₹650 cr: Secunderabad and Rajahmundry II completion, Kondapur's two extra floors (₹50-75 cr), maintenance, and a first tranche for the greenfields management says it will announce in FY28 (no revenue from them before FY30). FY26 capex was ₹1,428 cr (cash) plus ₹363 cr of new leases. Acquisitions are excluded (none agreed by 30-Sep-2026 with a price).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹283 cr (Screener) = 5.2% of average gross block, depressed because the new hospitals opened during the year and ₹21.5 cr of right-of-use depreciation was capitalised; Q1FY27 ₹101 cr (₹404 cr annualised) after Kondapur, Bengaluru and Palakkad. 6.25% gives FY27E ≈ ₹430 cr (PL ₹397 cr). The engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after borrowings, lease liabilities and minorities, which is negative. Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome`.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 2.18; Screener basis, which includes the associate's profit and exceptional items). FY27E ₹47 cr = Q1FY27 actual ₹17 cr + Q2-Q4: recurring non-treasury items ₹15.5 cr (FY26 run-rate ₹20.6 cr a year: interest on the KHL loan ₹3.9 cr, security deposits ₹2.3 cr, other loans ₹1.8 cr, government grants ₹3.5 cr, rent ₹1.6 cr, miscellaneous ₹7.5 cr) + associate share ₹2.4 cr + treasury ~₹13 cr (6.5% on ~₹270 cr average cash and funds left from the QIP, ₹505 cr at Jun-26 falling as it is spent). FY28E ₹36 cr and FY29E ₹38 cr: recurring ₹22-23 cr, associate ₹4-5 cr (KHL earns rent on the new Kondapur building), treasury ~₹10 cr on ~₹150 cr of working cash. One-offs left out (FY26 exceptional loss ₹11.2 cr; FY25 asset-sale gain ₹10.9 cr). FY26 ₹17 cr (₹28 cr before exceptional items); twelve months to Jun-26 ₹27 cr.

otherTreasury.label: Minority interests at book, counted as debt (shown negative)
otherTreasury._why: Engine workaround: Screener puts minority interests (book value ₹311 cr at Mar-26, AR FY26 note 2.10(c)) inside other liabilities, so the engine would treat them as a working-capital liability that grows with revenue. A negative other-treasury balance of ₹311 cr moves them out of working capital (operating working capital becomes ~8% of revenue, as reported: receivables, inventory and other assets less payables and other liabilities) and into net debt, identically in the engine and the Excel model. EV/EBITDA uses 100% of subsidiaries' EBITDA, so the minorities' claim belongs in net debt; the forward EV/EBITDA history is built the same way.

assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on bank debt, lease liabilities and other
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹215 cr (bank ₹162 cr, leases ₹35 cr, other ₹6 cr) with interest still being capitalised; Q1FY27 ₹83 cr on ~₹3,200 cr of bank debt before the QIP money arrived (24-Jun). Debt fell to ~₹2,400 cr by early August (₹1,125 cr repaid). FY27E = Q1 ₹83 cr + ~₹63 cr a quarter (₹2,300-2,400 cr at ~8.5-9%, plus ~₹42 cr a year on leases). FY28E-29E: debt falls to ~₹1,700 cr and ~₹1,100 cr as the warrant money (₹450 cr) comes in and free cash flow turns positive. PL: ₹280 / 230 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Attributable profit was 70-74% of PBT in FY23-25 (tax ~26%, minorities 7-8% of profit), 72% in FY26 and 74% in Q1FY27 (tax 34%, but minorities absorbed ₹4 cr of Bengaluru/Nashik losses). As those units turn profitable the minorities' share rises: we assume tax ~28% / 26% / 25.5% and minorities ~3% / 6% / 7.5% of PBT (≈3% / 8% / 10% of profit; management: 10-15% long term).
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend since listing; cash goes to expansion and debt reduction.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity. Net debt including leases and minorities is ~8% of enterprise value after the QIP, so WACC (~11.3-11.4%) is close to the 11.3% that beta 0.8 gives; hospitals are defensive, but KIMS carries execution risk in four new states.
dcf._tgWhy: Under-bedded country, rising insurance and ageing: 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~18% to 9% by year 15 as the network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 26% post-Ind AS: mature clusters earn ~30% (Telangana) and ~25% (AP), but a growing share of beds in costlier markets with higher rents (Kerala 20-22% at maturity, Maharashtra, Bengaluru) and continuing openings keep the blend below the 26% of FY24-25.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex including new leases falls from ~9-10% of revenue to 8%: replacement (depreciation ~6.5% of revenue) plus beds for 6-9% growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Kondapur reaches ₹70-80 cr a month by FY29, Bengaluru and Thane hit mid-teens margins a year early, Kerala reaches 20%, and the call options on O&M hospitals add profitable beds; margin toward 25% by FY29 (company target ~30% by FY30).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Insurer empanelment stays slow, Kondapur and the new states fill at half the pace, and a new round of greenfields restarts losses; margin stuck near 20-21% and debt rises again.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values KIMS: EV/EBITDA on FY28E (Prabhudas Lilladher 30x and Axis Securities 27x after Q1FY27; ICICI Direct used 30x FY27E in 2025). We use post-Ind AS EBITDA before other income (the model and Screener basis) with lease liabilities and minority interests (book) in net debt. 19.5x = KIMS's 21.8x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since listing (Jun-2021; no trough years: forward EBITDA never fell below half its prior peak), cut by the 11.5% median de-rating of seven listed hospital peers versus their five-year median EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo −13.5%, Max −13.0%, Fortis +0.4%, Narayana −1.8%, Medanta +4.3%, Rainbow −11.5%, Jupiter −24.2%; KIMS itself excluded, Aster left out because its 2024 GCC demerger distorts its history) = 19.3x, rounded to 19.5x. On EBITDA before start-up losses the median is 20.2x (17.9x after de-rating), a lower value; we use the reported basis because KIMS opens hospitals every year, so some start-up drag is permanent. No growth premium: faster EBITDA growth (~28% a year FY26-29E) mostly reverses FY26's start-up losses and comes with returns at or below the cost of equity until FY29E. Bull 26.5x and bear 17.5x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of its forward EV/EBITDA since listing.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings. 38x = KIMS's 43.6x median one-year-forward P/E since listing (forwardMedian; no trough years by the house rule, though FY26-27 EPS are depressed by start-up losses and interest) cut by the 12.1% median P/E de-rating of the same seven peers (38.3x). Bull 52x, bear 34x scale with the EV/EBITDA multiples.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (capex includes new leases), Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, less net debt including leases and minorities (book).

cover.headline: Telangana's leading hospital chain, mid-way through a five-state build-out: the market already pays for the new beds to fill
cover.lead: KIMS runs 26 multi-specialty hospitals (7,459 beds, 5,639 operational) at tier-2 prices: its mature hospitals in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh earn 25-30% EBITDA margins at an ARPOB of ₹47,200, a fraction of metro chains'. Since FY24 it has added ~3,500 beds in four new states, which cut the FY26 margin to 21% (new units lost ₹128 cr), pushed net debt to 5.4x EBITDA and forced a ₹1,500 cr QIP and ₹600 cr of promoter warrants in Jun-Aug 2026. Q1FY27 revenue rose 35%, EBITDA 16%; profit fell 47%. The street values KIMS on **EV/EBITDA on FY28E (27-30x)**. We forecast EBITDA of ₹1,057 / 1,366 / 1,716 cr and EPS of ₹6.5 / 11.4 / 16.6 for FY27-29E (42.77 cr fully diluted shares). Applying **19.5x to Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,541 cr** (post-Ind AS; leases and minorities in net debt) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: P/E ₹533, DCF ₹579. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Telangana (half of revenue, ~77% of EBITDA in Q1FY27) earns ~30% margins and Andhra Pradesh 21-25% at an ARPOB of only ~₹25,000. Doctor-partners own equity in ten hospital companies, which helps recruitment but leaks profit to minorities (₹30 cr in FY25).

arguments.h: The new hospitals are turning, one by one
arguments.p: Nashik broke even and Mahadevapura turned positive in Q1FY27; Bengaluru's loss halved to ₹19 cr; Electronic City (−₹18 cr) and Thane (−₹7 cr) are next. We assume new-unit losses fall from ₹128 cr to ₹60 cr in FY27E and model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}} from a five-cluster build.

arguments.h: Repaired with equity, not cash flow
arguments.p: Net debt including leases and minorities was ₹4,386 cr at Mar-26 (5.4x EBITDA); the QIP and warrants (7% dilution) cut it to ~₹2,310 cr pro forma. Promoters pledged another 6.67% of the company on 18-Sep-2026, and management plans new greenfields from FY28. Our margin ({{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} in FY28E) is below PL and Axis.

arguments.h: Valuation: the recovery is in the price
arguments.p: At ₹746 KIMS trades at 25.1x our FY28E EV/EBITDA, above its 21.8x forward median since listing, while hospital peers sit ~11% below their own medians. 19.5x on Sep-28E gives ₹660; the street's 27-30x would be ₹818-914. P/E and DCF are lower still.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with lower interest after the QIP repayments, Thane and Electronic City breakeven, Kondapur's ramp and Bengaluru's path to an EBITDA-neutral year.
Thrissur O&M hospital (351 beds) due within 3-4 months of Aug-2026; Secunderabad replacement block by end-CY27; Rajahmundry II under construction.
Call options on O&M hospitals exercisable from Jan-2027, and the new greenfield or acquisition projects management expects to announce in FY28.
Conversion of the promoter warrants (₹450 cr due within 18 months of Aug-2026) and any further change in promoter pledges.
Insurer empanelment of Thane, Nashik and the Bengaluru hospitals (key panels expected by mid-September 2026).

sections.title: Multi-specialty hospitals at tier-2 prices, built in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, now in five states

blocks.p: KIMS runs general multi-specialty hospitals that do complex (tertiary) work: cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, joint replacement, kidney care, gastroenterology, cancer care and heart, lung, liver and kidney transplants. Its formula, set by the founder Dr B. Bhaskara Rao (a cardio-thoracic surgeon who helped design Andhra Pradesh's Aarogyasri health scheme in 2007), is big hospitals at "affordable" prices in second-tier cities, run with full-time doctors, many of whom own equity in the local hospital company. Revenue per occupied bed-day (ARPOB) was ₹47,200 in Q1FY27, far below metro chains, yet the mature Telangana hospitals earn ~30% EBITDA margins.

In FY26 hospital services brought in ₹2,653 cr, pharmacy ₹1,202 cr and other income from operations (academic courses, food, O&M fees) ₹49 cr. Cash-paying patients are 52% of revenue, insurers 32%, corporates and government health plans (CGHS, PSUs) 12% and the Aarogyasri scheme only 4% (Q1FY27). No single specialty dominates: cardiac and orthopaedics 15% each, neurosciences 11%, renal, gastro and mother & child 9% each, oncology 7%, transplants 3%.

sections.title: A growing, under-bedded market, but the bed boom is now in KIMS's home city

blocks.p: ICRA's sample of listed and unlisted hospital chains (30-Jul-2026): revenue growth of 13-15% in FY27 and 15-17% in FY28, cut from 18-20% for FY27 in its Dec-2025 update; FY26 occupancy 63.5%; ARPOB +6-8% in FY27 after +9.2% in FY26; operating margin 22-24% in FY27-28 (24.1% in FY26); outlook Positive. ICRA (Jul-2025) expected the sector to add ~14,500 beds for ₹30,000-32,000 cr of capex by FY27. For KIMS three things matter more than the national average: competition for patients and doctors in Hyderabad, where several large hospitals opened in the last year; insurers' willingness to empanel new hospitals quickly, which slowed every one of KIMS's FY26 openings; and the price point of tier-2 Andhra Pradesh, where ARPOB is a third of Hyderabad's.

sections.title: Five clusters, two of them earning the money: Telangana and Andhra make all the EBITDA

blocks.p: Hospital revenue is operational beds × occupancy × ARPOB (revenue per occupied bed-day, which at KIMS includes outpatient and pharmacy revenue). The five clusters are very different businesses. **Telangana** (Hyderabad: Secunderabad, Kondapur, the two Sunshine hospitals) charges ~₹77,000 a bed-day and earns ~30%. **Andhra Pradesh** (eight hospitals in smaller towns) charges only ~₹25,000 and still earns 21-25%, the cheapest tertiary care in the listed sector. **Maharashtra** (Nagpur, Nashik, Thane), **Kerala** (Kannur, Kollam, Palakkad) and **Karnataka** (two Bengaluru hospitals) are 1-4 years old and earned nothing between them in FY26 (−₹88 cr of EBITDA).

sections.title: The new hospitals cost ₹128 cr of EBITDA in FY26; Q1FY27 shows them turning, one by one

blocks.p: This is the central question for KIMS. In FY26 its mature hospitals earned ₹956 cr of EBITDA on ₹3,335 cr of revenue (~29%), while units in their first year lost ₹128 cr on ₹597 cr (FY25: −₹18.3 cr). Without those losses FY26 EBITDA would have been ~₹943 cr, up 19% rather than 3%. The good news in Q1FY27: Nashik broke even, Mahadevapura (Bengaluru) was EBITDA-positive from June, Vizag QNRI (acquired loss-making in 2024) reached a ~16% margin and Kerala made money. The bad news: Electronic City still lost ~₹18 cr in the quarter, Thane ~₹7 cr, and the 787-bed Kondapur hospital and Thrissur start the cycle again.

Management's FY27 promise (Bengaluru cluster EBITDA-neutral for the year) needs Electronic City to break even by the second half. We assume new-unit losses roughly halve in FY27 (₹60 cr) and fall to ₹25-30 cr a year after that, with new openings replacing the old.

sections.title: Pipeline: fill the beds already built, then O&M and a new round of greenfields

blocks.p: After adding ~3,500 beds in two and a half years, KIMS says the next eight months are about stabilising what it has built: filling the 787-bed Kondapur hospital (₹45 cr in July versus ₹32-33 cr a month at the old site; potential ~₹100 cr a month in 4-5 years), finishing the Secunderabad replacement block (end-CY27) and Rajahmundry II, and opening Thrissur under an O&M contract. It is also growing asset-light: in Aug-Sep 2026 it signed O&M agreements for Arete Hospital in Gachibowli (250 beds) and a 183-bed hospital in Kakinada, both for 9% of revenue, with options to buy later. New greenfield projects are likely to be announced in FY28, only in its existing states (plus one hospital in Chennai).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh KIMS has a genuine advantage: dense networks, doctor loyalty built through equity partnerships, and a cost structure that earns 25-30% margins at prices well below the metro chains. That moat does **not** travel automatically. In Bengaluru, Thane and Kerala KIMS is a new entrant competing against established chains, and FY26 showed it lacks bargaining power with insurers for new hospitals. The low-price model is also a ceiling: KIMS's ARPOB is about half that of the metro-focused chains, so its margin upside comes from filling beds, not from price.

sections.title: Revenue tripled since FY21, but profit fell in FY26 as ten new hospitals opened

blocks.p: KIMS grew revenue from ₹1,330 cr in FY21 to ₹3,905 cr in FY26 (24% a year), with acquisitions (Sunshine and Nagpur in 2022, Vizag QNRI in 2024) and a five-state building programme. Margins tell the other half of the story: EBITDA was 32% of revenue in FY22 (a Covid-era peak), 26% in FY24-25 and only 20.9% in FY26, when Thane, two Bengaluru hospitals, Kerala and several O&M units opened in the same year and lost ₹128 cr of EBITDA between them. Profit attributable to shareholders fell 37% to ₹241 cr in FY26 because depreciation and interest on the new hospitals arrived before their revenue: depreciation rose from ₹177 cr to ₹283 cr and interest from ₹100 cr to ₹215 cr.

sections.title: Expansion paid for with debt, then with new shares: ₹2,400 cr of capex in two years

blocks.p: Over FY25-26 KIMS generated ₹1,093 cr of operating cash but spent ₹2,437 cr on capex, ₹176 cr on acquisitions and O&M deals, ₹250 cr buying out doctor-partners (mainly Sunshine), and ₹363 cr on interest and lease interest. The gap, ₹2,123 cr, was borrowed: bank debt rose from ₹1,047 cr (Mar-24) to ₹3,244 cr (Mar-26). Returns fell with it: ROCE (Screener) was 34% in FY22, 17% in FY24 and 10% in FY26. In June 2026 KIMS raised ₹1,500 cr in a QIP and in August its promoters subscribed to ₹600 cr of warrants; ₹1,125 cr of debt was repaid by early July. Management says the next three to four years of operating cash (₹2,000-2,500 cr) will go into new greenfield and brownfield hospitals in its existing states.

sections.title: Earnings quality: read the EBITDA definitions, the minorities and the related-party Kondapur structure

bullets: **Three EBITDA numbers.** The company's "EBITDA" includes other income (FY26 ₹828 cr, 21.1%); Screener's and ours excludes it (₹815 cr, 20.9%); both are post-Ind AS 116, i.e. before rent. Pre-Ind AS (after rent) it was ₹785 cr including other income. Rent is small for KIMS (₹44 cr in FY26) because it owns most hospitals, but rising (₹18 cr in Q1FY27).
**Doctors sit in other expenses.** Consultancy charges to doctors were ₹1,007 cr (25.8% of revenue) on top of ₹682 cr of employee cost.

**Capitalisation is unwinding.** In FY26 ₹34 cr of lease interest and ₹21.5 cr of right-of-use depreciation were capitalised into projects; as hospitals open these move into the P&L, which is why profit lags EBITDA in FY27.

**Minorities.** Ten hospital companies have doctor-partners (stakes 51-91%). Their share of profit fell from ₹30 cr (FY25) to ₹0.6 cr (FY26) because they share Bengaluru and Nashik losses; it rises again as those turn profitable (management: 10-15% of profit long term). We report profit attributable to owners throughout and count minorities at book (₹311 cr) in net debt.

**O&M accounting.** Kannur and Kollam are consolidated as business combinations (right-of-use assets, contingent consideration); Sangli, Guntur and Kompally earn a fee and sit outside the bed KPIs; call options on O&M hospital companies are fair-valued through P&L (−₹3.8 cr in FY26).
**One-offs.** FY25 included a ₹12 cr land sale in revenue and EBITDA and a ₹10.9 cr asset-sale gain; FY26 an ₹11.2 cr exceptional loss and a ₹46 cr deferred-tax credit.
**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was 63% of EBITDA in FY26 (73% in FY25) as receivables grew faster than revenue (52 days, from 28 in FY22).

**Related parties.** The new 787-bed Kondapur hospital building belongs to Kondapur Healthcare Ltd, a 40.5% associate that KIMS has also lent ₹68.8 cr (12%); who owns the other 59.5% is not disclosed in what we read. In FY25 KIMS sold land for ₹45 cr to a company of KMP relatives. Small in value, but they deserve scrutiny.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Disclosure is good (cluster P&Ls every quarter, unit charts for new hospitals) and the auditor (S.R. Batliboi, EY) is clean. The amber is for structure: three EBITDA definitions in circulation, profit leaking to minorities, capitalised costs now unwinding, an associate-owned flagship building and slow receivables.

sections.title: Net debt peaked at 5.4x EBITDA in March 2026; the QIP and warrants cut it to ~2.8x

blocks.p: At March 2026 KIMS owed ₹3,244 cr to banks, had ₹1,009 cr of lease liabilities (leased hospitals in Kerala, Thane and Bengaluru, and right-of-use assets under the Kerala O&M agreements) and ₹311 cr of minority partners' equity in its subsidiaries, against only ₹178 cr of cash, funds and investments (including ₹88 cr in the associate that owns the new Kondapur building). That is net debt of ₹4,386 cr on our basis, 5.4x FY26 EBITDA. Adding the QIP proceeds (₹1,476 cr net) and all ₹600 cr of the warrant money gives a pro forma ₹2,310 cr, 2.8x FY26 and ~2.2x our FY27E EBITDA. The company reported debt of ₹2,570 cr at June 2026 and ~₹2,400 cr in early August (excluding leases), and targets ~2x net debt/EBITDA.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for KIMS (consolidated, ₹ crore). One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and a post-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin excluding other income (Screener basis: rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest sits in interest and right-of-use depreciation in depreciation; lease liabilities sit in borrowings). The cluster build (five states: beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB, plus O&M fees less eliminations) sits in `businessLines`; the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue and that cluster EBITDA reconciles to model EBITDA. Profit is attributable to owners and the share count is pro forma for the Jun-2026 QIP and the Aug-2026 promoter warrants (fully diluted 42.77 cr; KIMS.patch.js); minority interests (book) sit in net debt and their share of profit in the tax line. Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the cluster build below. FY27 +32%: Q1 +35% (new Kondapur open only 10 days; Palakkad from April), the new Kondapur hospital running ~₹12 cr a month above the old one from July, Bengaluru, Thane and Kerala ramping, and the FY26 base still missing a full year of Mahadevapura and Electronic City. FY28 +20%: occupancy gains at Kondapur, Bengaluru and Kerala (Thrissur O&M from late FY27), ARPOB +4-5% (management guide). FY29 +18%: the Secunderabad replacement block (end-CY27) and Rajahmundry II start. No unannounced acquisitions or greenfields are included. Street: PL ₹5,111 / 6,152 cr, Axis ₹5,264 / 6,222 cr for FY27-28E.

businessLines._why: Revenue by state cluster = average operational beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB (company definitions; the identity reproduces Q1FY27 cluster revenue within ~1%). Telangana: 2,144 operational beds at Jun-26 including ~450 new Kondapur beds (open 10 days) and excluding ~200 Secunderabad beds under rebuild; occupancy dips to 45% in FY27 (Q1 41.1% on the enlarged base; 61-65% on the old base) and recovers as Kondapur fills (management: ~70% in 3-4 years); ARPOB +8% in FY27 (oncology and transplants at Kondapur; Q1 ₹77,009, +10%), then +4-5%. AP: Rajahmundry II adds beds in FY29; ARPOB base ₹26,000-27,000 (management). Maharashtra: Thane and Nashik ramp (Q1 occupancy 58.6%, July Thane revenue ₹21 cr a month). Kerala: Palakkad full year, Thrissur (O&M, 351 beds) from late FY27. Karnataka: ARPOB normalises to ₹80,000-85,000 (management) as empanelments widen; occupancy 33% → 48%. Other = O&M fees (9% of revenue at Sangli, Guntur, Kompally, Arete and Kakinada) less intercompany eliminations (~1% of cluster revenue). Cluster EBITDA margins are on the company basis (including other income); the reconciling line to model EBITDA (other income in cluster figures, O&M fees, classification) runs at −₹33 to −43 cr a year.
businessLines._startupWhy: EBITDA losses of units in their first year or two, already inside the cluster margins (used only for the start-up-adjusted multiple): FY27 Electronic City, Thane (H1), Kondapur transition (old-hospital rent and pre-operative costs), Palakkad and Thrissur start-up ~₹60 cr (management: 'less than half' of FY26's ₹128 cr); FY28 Thrissur and the extra Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ~₹25 cr; FY29 Rajahmundry II and Secunderabad ~₹30 cr.

assumptions._marginWhy: Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin excluding other income (Screener basis): 26% in FY24-25, 20.9% in FY26 (new-unit losses ₹128 cr), 18.9% in Q1FY27 (Q4FY26 19.2%). FY27 20.5%: Bengaluru losses shrink (Q1 −₹19 cr vs Q4FY26 −₹40 cr; cluster guided EBITDA-neutral for the year), Thane breaks even, Nashik positive, offset by the Kondapur transition and Kerala's single-digit margins. FY28 22.0% and FY29 23.5%: new clusters move to mid-teens (Kerala guided mid-teens FY28; Maharashtra 12-15%), Telangana back to ~30%, but new beds at Kondapur, Secunderabad and Rajahmundry keep dragging. Below PL (20.8% / 22.7%) and Axis (22.6% / 23.4%). Rent (Ind AS 116 impact ₹44 cr in FY26, ₹18 cr in Q1FY27) is ~1.5pp of revenue: pre-Ind AS ≈ 19.0% / 20.6% / 22.2%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex plus new leases (right-of-use additions, because lease liabilities are in net debt). FY27 ₹460 cr: Q1 ₹60-75 cr, ₹100-125 cr guided for the next nine months (Secunderabad, Rajahmundry II ₹60-75 cr, residual Kondapur), maintenance ~₹100 cr a year, Thrissur/Palakkad fit-outs and equipment, ~₹60 cr of new leases. FY28 ₹600 cr and FY29 ₹650 cr: Secunderabad and Rajahmundry II completion, Kondapur's two extra floors (₹50-75 cr), maintenance, and a first tranche for the greenfields management says it will announce in FY28 (no revenue from them before FY30). FY26 capex was ₹1,428 cr (cash) plus ₹363 cr of new leases. Acquisitions are excluded (none agreed by 30-Sep-2026 with a price).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹283 cr (Screener) = 5.2% of average gross block, depressed because the new hospitals opened during the year and ₹21.5 cr of right-of-use depreciation was capitalised; Q1FY27 ₹101 cr (₹404 cr annualised) after Kondapur, Bengaluru and Palakkad. 6.25% gives FY27E ≈ ₹430 cr (PL ₹397 cr). The engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after borrowings, lease liabilities and minorities, which is negative. Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome`.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 2.18; Screener basis, which includes the associate's profit and exceptional items). FY27E ₹47 cr = Q1FY27 actual ₹17 cr + Q2-Q4: recurring non-treasury items ₹15.5 cr (FY26 run-rate ₹20.6 cr a year: interest on the KHL loan ₹3.9 cr, security deposits ₹2.3 cr, other loans ₹1.8 cr, government grants ₹3.5 cr, rent ₹1.6 cr, miscellaneous ₹7.5 cr) + associate share ₹2.4 cr + treasury ~₹13 cr (6.5% on ~₹270 cr average cash and funds left from the QIP, ₹505 cr at Jun-26 falling as it is spent). FY28E ₹36 cr and FY29E ₹38 cr: recurring ₹22-23 cr, associate ₹4-5 cr (KHL earns rent on the new Kondapur building), treasury ~₹10 cr on ~₹150 cr of working cash. otherTreasury.label: Minority interests at book, counted as debt (shown negative)
otherTreasury._why: Engine workaround: Screener puts minority interests (book value ₹311 cr at Mar-26, AR FY26 note 2.10(c)) inside other liabilities, so the engine would treat them as a working-capital liability that grows with revenue. A negative other-treasury balance of ₹311 cr moves them out of working capital (operating working capital becomes ~8% of revenue, as reported: receivables, inventory and other assets less payables and other liabilities) and into net debt, identically in the engine and the Excel model. EV/EBITDA uses 100% of subsidiaries' EBITDA, so the minorities' claim belongs in net debt; the forward EV/EBITDA history is built the same way.

assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on bank debt, lease liabilities and other
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹215 cr (bank ₹162 cr, leases ₹35 cr, other ₹6 cr) with interest still being capitalised; Q1FY27 ₹83 cr on ~₹3,200 cr of bank debt before the QIP money arrived (24-Jun). Debt fell to ~₹2,400 cr by early August (₹1,125 cr repaid). FY27E = Q1 ₹83 cr + ~₹63 cr a quarter (₹2,300-2,400 cr at ~8.5-9%, plus ~₹42 cr a year on leases). FY28E-29E: debt falls to ~₹1,700 cr and ~₹1,100 cr as the warrant money (₹450 cr) comes in and free cash flow turns positive. PL: ₹280 / 230 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Attributable profit was 70-74% of PBT in FY23-25 (tax ~26%, minorities 7-8% of profit), 72% in FY26 and 74% in Q1FY27 (tax 34%, but minorities absorbed ₹4 cr of Bengaluru/Nashik losses). As those units turn profitable the minorities' share rises: we assume tax ~28% / 26% / 25.5% and minorities ~3% / 6% / 7.5% of PBT (≈3% / 8% / 10% of profit; management: 10-15% long term).
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend since listing; cash goes to expansion and debt reduction.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity. Net debt including leases and minorities is ~8% of enterprise value after the QIP, so WACC (~11.3-11.4%) is close to the 11.3% that beta 0.8 gives; hospitals are defensive, but KIMS carries execution risk in four new states.
dcf._tgWhy: Under-bedded country, rising insurance and ageing: 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~18% to 9% by year 15 as the network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 26% post-Ind AS: mature clusters earn ~30% (Telangana) and ~25% (AP), but a growing share of beds in costlier markets with higher rents (Kerala 20-22% at maturity, Maharashtra, Bengaluru) and continuing openings keep the blend below the 26% of FY24-25.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex including new leases falls from ~9-10% of revenue to 8%: replacement (depreciation ~6.5% of revenue) plus beds for 6-9% growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Kondapur reaches ₹70-80 cr a month by FY29, Bengaluru and Thane hit mid-teens margins a year early, Kerala reaches 20%, and the call options on O&M hospitals add profitable beds; margin toward 25% by FY29 (company target ~30% by FY30).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Insurer empanelment stays slow, Kondapur and the new states fill at half the pace, and a new round of greenfields restarts losses; margin stuck near 20-21% and debt rises again.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values KIMS: EV/EBITDA on FY28E (Prabhudas Lilladher 30x and Axis Securities 27x after Q1FY27; ICICI Direct used 30x FY27E in 2025). We use post-Ind AS EBITDA before other income (the model and Screener basis) with lease liabilities and minority interests (book) in net debt. 19.5x = KIMS's 21.8x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since listing (Jun-2021; no trough years: forward EBITDA never fell below half its prior peak), cut by the 11.5% median de-rating of seven listed hospital peers versus their five-year median EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo −13.5%, Max −13.0%, Fortis +0.4%, Narayana −1.8%, Medanta +4.3%, Rainbow −11.5%, Jupiter −24.2%; KIMS itself excluded, Aster left out because its 2024 GCC demerger distorts its history) = 19.3x, rounded to 19.5x. On EBITDA before start-up losses the median is 20.2x (17.9x after de-rating), a lower value; we use the reported basis because KIMS opens hospitals every year, so some start-up drag is permanent. No growth premium: faster EBITDA growth (~28% a year FY26-29E) mostly reverses FY26's start-up losses and comes with returns at or below the cost of equity until FY29E. Bull 26.5x and bear 17.5x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of its forward EV/EBITDA since listing.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings. 38x = KIMS's 43.6x median one-year-forward P/E since listing (forwardMedian; no trough years by the house rule, though FY26-27 EPS are depressed by start-up losses and interest) cut by the 12.1% median P/E de-rating of the same seven peers (38.3x). Bull 52x, bear 34x scale with the EV/EBITDA multiples.
